title: DNA Quantitation from PCR
author: Michael Van Dyke
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k5pcy5n

steps.title: Prepare Working Reagent (WR1)
steps.instruction: Dilute Quant‑iT™ dsDNA HS reagent 1:200 with Quant‑iT™ dsDNA buffer to a final volume equal to 200 µL × 1.1 × (number of assays). For example, for 10 assays prepare 1100 µL of WR1 in a polypropylene microcentrifuge tube, vortex briefly to mix, store shielded from direct light at room temperature, and use within 3 h. If desired, water can replace the buffer, but dsDNA values will be ~33 % lower.

steps.title: Label and Arrange Tubes
steps.instruction: Label high‑clarity 0.5 mL polypropylene microcentrifuge tubes (e.g., Axygen thin‑wall PCR tubes, part number PCR‑05‑C) on their caps, include a blank if desired, and place the tubes in a rack (a used 1000 µL pipet tip rack works well).

steps.title: Add Reagents and Incubate
steps.instruction: Aliquot 200 µL of WR1 into each labeled tube, add 2 µL of the completed PCR reaction, vortex briefly to mix, centrifuge briefly to coalesce the liquid, return tubes to the rack, and incubate at room temperature for at least 5 min (fluorescence may increase ≤10 % with time but remains stable for ≥1 h).

steps.title: Set Up Qubit Fluorometer
steps.instruction: Turn on the Qubit™ 2.0 fluorometer. On the touchscreen select “Choose Your Assay: DNA”, then “dsDNA High Sensitivity”. When prompted “Read New Standards?”, choose Yes if standards are to be measured, otherwise No. Note that the Quant‑iT™ dsDNA HS reagent has an excitation maximum of 502 nm (blue) and an emission maximum of 523 nm (green).

steps.title: Measure Samples
steps.instruction: Insert each sample tube into the Qubit, close the lid, and press “Read Next Sample”. Record the displayed values by hand or upload them to a USB flash drive after all readings are complete.

steps.title: Calculate Sample Concentrations
steps.instruction: Values displayed are for the WR1 dilution and are in ng/mL. Multiply each value by 100 to obtain the dsDNA concentration in the original PCR reaction in ng/µL. Typical yields for NEB Taq‑based 63‑bp PCR products are 3–6 ng/µL; blank samples usually give 1–1.5 ng/µL. Results may vary with primer concentration, sequence, and amplicon length.
